synopsis: Correlation is a prerequisite for credible simulation, not a substitute for physical testing: credibility applies only to dimensions with adequate paired simulation-to-real agreement, and Euro NCAP’s 2026 protocol, version 1.00 dated March 2025, requires correlation before predictions plus random physical verification [f7375, f1215, f1719]. Agreement must be assessed with multiple metrics and bounded by operating regimes, configuration and pre-agreed tolerances; a camera model may agree in daylight but fail under glare [f188, f7552, f9934, f7469]. Physical evidence shows both achievable agreement and important limits: underground stop-zone repeats agreed within about ±13 cm, while an on-road 2026 round robin still showed tool disagreements of 0.033 s and 0.314 m in a prescribed brake-only test [f5930, f6351]. The proposed programme should own correlation data in-house, use real sensors and machines for correlation, and gate progress on evidence rather than calendar dates; the four-month window cannot accommodate all correlation and other validation needs, and missing agreed metrics by the first quarter of 2027 is an early warning [f201, f10894, f9509, f378, f10756]. Remaining evidence gaps include unconfirmed simulated-to-real point-cloud comparison for the 2026 CARLA mining-dust framework and missing independent correlation results for Cognata and heavy-machine evidence for BeamNG.tech; large simulation counts cannot compensate for an uncorrelated model [f4743, f8415, f8509, f12203].
